sources.note: Keeping culture and Old objects: the 1851 exhibition, qualified provenance, 1984 reoccupation and 1995 land return.

sources.title: National Museum of Australia, Tasmanian Aboriginal shell necklaces
sources.note: Dulcie Greeno’s necklaces and the making process. Dated biographical language about living artists is not treated as a current status report.

sources.title: National Museum of Australia, Tasmanian bark canoe
sources.note: Historical descriptions and Rex Greeno’s reconstruction, including family participation. The museum’s modern canoe is not represented as an excavated ancient object.

sources.title: Aboriginal Land Council of Tasmania, Wybalenna
sources.note: Incarceration, the 1846 petition and continuing identity. Conflicting survivor totals on this and other pages are excluded.

sources.title: Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre, About palawa kani
sources.note: Community language program, evidence and reconstruction methods. Revived language is distinguished from any one of the original languages.

identityAssociations.locator: Palawa Story and Contemporary Palawa Community
identityAssociations.scope: The two imported labels name the same broad Tasmanian subject in non-consecutive snapshots. Their feature extents both cover Tasmania. This shared overview distinguishes archaeological evidence, local practices and continuing people; it does not identify every ancient community with one modern political unit.
